method_card.title: Jobs and Work Experience
method_card.content:
This lesson covers jobs vocabulary, the German feminine suffix -in, work experience, and giving opinions about future careers. It is built fresh from the German specification — there is no direct parallel in other board courses.

GermanEnglish
der Arzt / die Ärztindoctor (m/f)
der Lehrer / die Lehrerinteacher (m/f)
der Krankenpfleger / die Krankenschwesternurse (m/f)
der Ingenieur / die Ingenieurinengineer (m/f)
der Rechtsanwalt / die Rechtsanwältinlawyer (m/f)
der Koch / die Köchincook/chef (m/f)
der Verkäufer / die Verkäuferinshop assistant (m/f)
der Beruf, die Berufeprofession / job
das Praktikumwork experience / internship
die Firmacompany / firm
arbeitento work
Ich möchte ... werden.I would like to become ...

Grammar focus 1 — profession as predicate: NO article: In German, you do not use an article before a profession when it follows sein (to be) as a predicate. Say Ich bin Lehrer (I am a teacher), NOT Ich bin ein Lehrer. However, if you add an adjective, the article returns: Ich bin ein guter Lehrer.

Grammar focus 2 — feminine forms with -in: Most male job titles become feminine by adding -in: der Lehrer → die Lehrerin, der Arzt → die Ärztin (with umlaut), der Koch → die Köchin (with umlaut). This suffix is a key feature of German and must be used correctly when referring to women.

Grammar focus 3 — future with möchte/will/werden: Three ways to express future plans: (1) Ich möchte Ärztin werden (I would like to become a doctor — modal + infinitive at end); (2) Ich werde Ingenieur (I will be an engineer — werden present = future); (3) present tense + future adverb: Nächstes Jahr mache ich ein Praktikum.

Model paragraph: Ich möchte in der Zukunft Ärztin werden, weil ich Menschen helfen möchte. Letzten Sommer habe ich ein Praktikum bei einer Firma gemacht. Ich fand es interessant, obwohl es manchmal stressig war.
(I would like to become a doctor in the future because I would like to help people. Last summer I did work experience at a company. I found it interesting, although it was sometimes stressful.)
steps: Learn jobs vocabulary with correct genders and feminine -in forms (Lehrerin, Ärztin, Köchin)
Use sein + profession WITHOUT an article: Ich bin Lehrer — not Ich bin ein Lehrer
Express future career plans with möchte/will + werden (infinitive at end of clause)
Talk about work experience (Praktikum) using the perfect tense: Ich habe ein Praktikum gemacht
Give opinions about future careers using weil + verb at end and finden + adjective

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — future plans and work experience appear in writing tasks and speaking conversations about future opportunities

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Ich möchte in der Zukunft Ärztin werden.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ich möchte = I would like. This is a modal verb (conditional form of mögen).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: in der Zukunft = in the future. This is a dative phrase (dative after the preposition in for time).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Ärztin werden = to become a doctor (female). The infinitive werden goes to the end after the modal.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I would like to become a doctor in the future.

worked_examples.question: Why is 'Ich bin Lehrer' correct but 'Ich bin ein Lehrer' is wrong (without an adjective)?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: In English, you say 'I am a teacher.' You need the indefinite article 'a'.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: In German, when a profession follows sein (to be) as a predicate and no adjective is present, the article is dropped. This is a German-specific rule with no English parallel.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Correct: Ich bin Lehrer. (I am a teacher — no article.) If you add an adjective: Ich bin ein guter Lehrer. (I am a good teacher — article returns.)

bronze.question: Match the German job titles to the English meaning
Match the German career and work experience words to the English meaning
Complete the sentence — profession after sein: no article needed

gaps.rule: Profession after sein — feminine form, no article
gaps.correct_explain: Ärztin is the feminine form of Arzt (doctor). After sein, no article: Sie ist Ärztin.

wrong.eine Ärztin: Do not use an article before a profession after ist (unless adding an adjective). Use Ärztin without eine.
wrong.Arzt: Arzt is the masculine form. Mutter is female: use the feminine form Ärztin.

gaps.rule: Profession after sein — masculine form, no article
gaps.correct_explain: Lehrer is the masculine form. After sein, no article: Er ist Lehrer.

wrong.ein Lehrer: Do not use an article before a profession after ist (unless adding an adjective).

bronze.question: Complete the sentence — möchte + infinitive at end
sentence_parts: Ich möchte in der Zukunft Ingenieurin

gaps.correct_explain: After möchte, the infinitive werden goes to the end of the clause.

wrong.werde: werde is the conjugated ich form of werden. After möchte, use the infinitive: werden.
wrong.wird: wird is the er/sie form. After möchte, use the infinitive: werden.

bronze.question: What does 'Ich habe letzten Sommer ein Praktikum gemacht' mean?
options: I did work experience last summer
I will do work experience next summer
I am doing work experience this summer
I enjoyed my work experience last summer

bronze.question: How do you say 'She is a nurse' in German? Choose the correct option.

bronze.source_text: Ich möchte Rechtsanwalt werden, weil ich fair und hilfsbereit bin.
model_answers: I would like to become a lawyer because I am fair and helpful.
I would like to be a lawyer because I am fair and helpful.

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear
bronze.translation: I would like to become a teacher (female).

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: I **would like** to become an engineer because I find technology **interesting**.

gaps.correct_explain: möchte (would like) or will (want to) both express a future wish. The infinitive werden sits at the end.

wrong.möchten: möchten is the wir/sie plural form. For ich, use möchte.

gaps.correct_explain: interessant means interesting. With finden, the adjective follows the noun: ich finde Technik interessant.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Mein Bruder möchte Arzt werden, weil er will Menschen helfen.
silver.error_type: Subordinate clause word order — modal at end
silver.explanation: After weil, both verbs go to the end of the subordinate clause, with the conjugated verb last: weil er Menschen helfen will.
silver.translation: My brother would like to become a doctor because he wants to help people.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: I did work experience at a company last summer.

distractor_labels.machte: wrong tense — machte is the simple past (imperfect). Use the perfect tense: habe ... gemacht.

silver.source_text: My sister would like to become a lawyer because she finds it interesting.
model_answers: Meine Schwester möchte Rechtsanwältin werden, weil sie es interessant findet.
hints: she finds it = sie findet es

model_answers: Ich möchte Ärztin werden, weil ich Menschen helfen möchte. Letztes Jahr habe ich ein Praktikum in einem Krankenhaus gemacht und ich fand es aufregend.

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: I would like to become a teacher because teaching is fun.

distractor_labels.ein Lehrer: wrong — after möchte werden, profession takes NO article. Use Lehrer, not ein Lehrer.
distractor_labels.machte: wrong tense — machte is simple past. Present tense macht is needed here (it makes fun = it is fun).

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a career event at school and are asked about your future career plans and any work experience you have done.

bullets.prompt: Say what job you would like to do in the future and give a reason.
bullets.model_answer: Ich möchte Ingenieurin werden, weil ich Mathematik und Naturwissenschaften interessant finde.
bullets.note: möchte + profession + werden (no article, infinitive at end), weil + verb at end

bullets.prompt: Describe any work experience you have done — where, when and what you thought of it.
bullets.model_answer: Letzten Sommer habe ich ein Praktikum bei einer Firma gemacht. Ich fand es sehr interessant und habe viel gelernt.
bullets.note: perfect tense + bei + dative, simple past fand is acceptable at Foundation for written reflection

bullets.prompt: Ask if there are any career opportunities in engineering at the event.
bullets.model_answer: Gibt es hier Informationen über Berufe im Bereich Ingenieurwesen?
bullets.note: Gibt es + accusative, über + accusative, polite question form

Mark on: Communication (job aspiration with reason, work experience, preference), Range of language (möchte/will + profession + werden with no article, perfect tense for past events, weil + verb-final, opinion structures), Accuracy (profession without article after sein/werden, feminine -in forms, perfect tense haben + past participle, verb-final in weil/dass clauses, noun capitalisation). Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}
